scope: Primary literature and official resources supporting the workflow and its limitations. No source validates Cedar Trace, converts its synthetic results into field evidence, or supplies an unmeasured ecological or life-cycle outcome.

cedar_trace_boundary.measures: Synthetic, model-computed hydraulic and runoff-accounting quantities under the checked-in SWMM assumptions.
does_not_measure: Pollutant loads, pollutant removal, or receiving-water quality.
Groundwater recharge; SWMM infiltration loss is a runoff-accounting term, not a field recharge measurement.
Air temperature, surface temperature, or heat-island reduction.
Real flood probability, property damage, or avoided flood risk.
Materials, construction, transport, maintenance, replacement, end-of-life, or embodied carbon.
Measured computational energy or carbon emissions.
cedar_trace_boundary.interpretation: EPA describes potential green-infrastructure benefit categories, while life-cycle studies show that benefits and burdens depend on site conditions, functional units, materials, construction, operation, maintenance, and end-of-life boundaries. Those outcomes require separate evidence ledgers and cannot be inferred from Cedar Trace hydraulics.

sources.title: Storm Water Management Model User's Manual Version 5.2
sources.supports: SWMM's rainfall-runoff and routing scope, LID representation, input/report/output workflow, continuity diagnostics, and the need for calibration data.
sources.does_not_support: That a particular model is calibrated, fit for a site decision, regulator-approved, or design-ready.

sources.title: Multiobjective optimization of low impact development stormwater controls
sources.authors: Kyle Eckart; Zach McPhee; Tirupati Bolisetti
sources.supports: Coupling a calibrated SWMM model to multiobjective search to expose cost, peak-flow, and runoff-volume tradeoffs over multiple return periods.
sources.does_not_support: Generalizing one Windsor sewershed's reductions or treating every nondominated alternative as professionally acceptable.

sources.title: Environmental Benefits of Green Infrastructure
sources.supports: Potential green-infrastructure benefit categories, including runoff capture and slowing, water-quality improvement, groundwater recharge where site conditions allow, heat-island reduction, and habitat connectivity.
sources.does_not_support: That Cedar Trace measures any of those field outcomes, that every GI practice provides every benefit, or that a modeled runoff change establishes real flood-risk reduction.

sources.title: Green Infrastructure and Groundwater Protection
sources.supports: Treating recharge and groundwater quality as site- and design-dependent outcomes that require soil, water-table, contaminant, siting, pretreatment, and monitoring evidence.
sources.does_not_support: Interpreting SWMM infiltration loss as measured groundwater recharge or assuming infiltration always improves groundwater quality.

sources.title: Multi-Objective Evolutionary Optimization and Monte Carlo Simulation for Placement of Low Impact Development in the Catchment Scale
sources.supports: The importance of placement and the use of SWMM-linked evolutionary search to characterize cost and flow-regime tradeoffs.
sources.does_not_support: A global-optimum claim for an incompletely evaluated or different candidate universe.

sources.title: Sensitivity of peak flow to the change of rainfall temporal pattern due to warmer climate
sources.authors: Samira Fadhel; Miguel Angel Rico-Ramirez; Dawei Han
sources.supports: Within-event rainfall timing, as well as volume, can change sewer-network peak-flow response.
sources.does_not_support: That Cedar Trace's synthetic storms have authoritative recurrence intervals or field probabilities.

sources.title: Calibration and Verification of SWMM for Low Impact Development
sources.authors: David J. Rosa; John C. Clausen; Michael E. Dietz
sources.supports: Separating numerical execution from calibration and verification evidence for LID modeling.
sources.does_not_support: Transferring the study's site-specific error magnitudes to other SWMM models.

sources.title: Do baseline assumptions alter the efficacy of green stormwater infrastructure to reduce combined sewer overflows?
sources.authors: Mayra Rodriguez; Giovan Battista Cavadini; Lauren M. Cook
sources.supports: Testing how evapotranspiration, upstream inflow, groundwater, and their interactions change modeled combined-sewer-overflow estimates and modeled GI effectiveness over a thirty-year Fehraltorf study.
sources.does_not_support: Treating any modeled reduction as observed field performance, ignoring the retained SWMM-report QA, or transferring Fehraltorf results to another catchment.

sources.title: Data for: Do baseline assumptions alter the efficacy of green stormwater infrastructure to reduce combined sewer overflows?
sources.supports: Hash-verifiable SWMM input packages, retained reports, published thirty-year result tables, and analysis code for the Fehraltorf model-structure case study.
sources.does_not_support: A fresh independent SWMM reproduction because the complete licensed meteorological forcing is not redistributed; nor does it establish field, ecological, regulatory, or construction outcomes.

sources.title: Green infrastructure life cycle assessment: A bio-infiltration case study
sources.authors: Kathleen M. Flynn; Robert G. Traver
sources.supports: A cradle-to-grave, site-specific LCA of a bio-infiltration rain garden that accounts for construction, operation, maintenance-related inputs, decommissioning, environmental impact categories, and life-cycle cost.
sources.does_not_support: Transferring the case study's impacts or benefits to Cedar Trace, inferring embodied carbon from hydraulic output, or omitting materials and end-of-life boundaries.

sources.title: Comparing Green and Grey Infrastructure Using Life Cycle Cost and Environmental Impact: A Rain Garden Case Study in Cincinnati, OH
sources.authors: Donald Vineyard; Wesley W. Ingwersen; Troy R. Hawkins; Xiaobo Xue; Bayou Demeke; William Shuster
sources.supports: Comparing a site-specific rain-garden program with grey infrastructure using explicit life-cycle environmental and cost boundaries, including material extraction, manufacturing, use, and disposal.
sources.does_not_support: Generalizing the Cincinnati comparison to Cedar Trace or claiming real environmental return on investment without a project-specific inventory and functional unit.

sources.title: Life Cycle Assessment modelling of stormwater treatment systems
sources.authors: Aisling D. O'Sullivan; Daniel Wicke; Tyler J. Hengen; Heidi L. Sieverding; James J. Stone
sources.supports: Evaluating stormwater-treatment impacts across materials, construction, transport, operation, and maintenance using an explicit functional unit and multiple environmental indicators.
sources.does_not_support: Assuming a hydraulically attractive alternative has low embodied or operating impact, or transferring one treatment system's footprint to a different site and design.

sources.title: A Fast and Elitist Multiobjective Genetic Algorithm: NSGA-II
sources.authors: Kalyanmoy Deb; Amrit Pratap; Sameer Agarwal; T. Meyarivan
sources.supports: Elitist nondominated sorting and diversity preservation as a multiobjective search baseline.
sources.does_not_support: That NSGA-II is universally best or that its observed frontier is globally complete.

sources.title: Performance Assessment of Multiobjective Optimizers: An Analysis and Review
sources.authors: Eckart Zitzler; Lothar Thiele; Marco Laumanns; Carlos M. Fonseca; Viviane Grunert da Fonseca
sources.supports: Assessing approximation sets with more than one quality perspective rather than declaring a winner from one scalar metric.
sources.does_not_support: A field-engineering conclusion from algorithm quality alone.

sources.title: Extremely Randomized Trees
sources.authors: Pierre Geurts; Damien Ernst; Louis Wehenkel
sources.supports: ExtraTrees as a computationally efficient randomized tree ensemble for regression and classification.
sources.does_not_support: That ExtraTrees improves GI search; that proposition must be tested in the controlled benchmark.

sources.title: Surrogate-based multiobjective optimization to rapidly size low impact development practices for outflow capture
sources.supports: Testing surrogate-assisted search as a way to reduce expensive simulator evaluations in an LID sizing study.
sources.does_not_support: Using surrogate predictions as engineering evidence, transferring one catchment's speedup, or assuming reliable extrapolation.

sources.title: Green Algorithms: Quantifying the Carbon Footprint of Computation
sources.authors: Loic Lannelongue; Jason Grealey; Michael Inouye
sources.supports: Transparent computational-footprint estimates based on runtime, processor and memory use, facility efficiency, and electricity carbon intensity.
sources.does_not_support: A full hardware lifecycle assessment or a carbon-savings claim when energy observations are unavailable.

sources.title: Towards the Systematic Reporting of the Energy and Carbon Footprints of Machine Learning
sources.supports: Reporting resource and energy context alongside model quality rather than treating accuracy as the only outcome.
sources.does_not_support: A universal carbon conversion factor independent of hardware, utilization, location, and accounting boundary.

sources.title: Green Infrastructure Modeling Toolkit
sources.supports: SWMM and cost/performance screening as established green-infrastructure planning categories.
sources.does_not_support: Automatic regulatory compliance or design approval.

sources.title: Beyond Accuracy: Behavioral Testing of NLP Models with CheckList
sources.authors: Marco Tulio Ribeiro; Tongshuang Wu; Carlos Guestrin; Sameer Singh
sources.supports: Testing concrete capabilities with invariance and directional-expectation cases instead of treating one aggregate accuracy score as a complete behavioral evaluation.
sources.does_not_support: That the R4c corpus measures general model capability, practitioner usefulness, or performance outside its fixed synthetic evidence-following tasks.

sources.title: Expanding the AI Evaluation Toolbox with Statistical Models
sources.authors: Andrew Keller; Kweku Kwegyir-Aggrey; Ryan Steed; Anita Rao; Julia Sharp; Amanda Bergman
sources.publisher: National Institute of Standards and Technology
sources.supports: Distinguishing performance conditioned on a fixed benchmark from generalized performance over a broader population of possible test items.
sources.does_not_support: Calling R4c generalized model accuracy or extrapolating its scenario counts beyond the frozen benchmark families that were actually tested.

sources.title: W&B Tables, Artifacts, lineage, and Reports
sources.supports: The observability primitives used to mirror exact tables, campaign runs, artifact versions, and report panels.
sources.does_not_support: Treating W&B as the hydraulic authority or allowing cloud state to change engineering results.

sources.title: W&B Weave agent tracing, evaluations, and structured inference
sources.supports: Grouping stable multi-turn conversations, tracing each turn with model and tool activity, recording token use and feedback, and comparing pinned model outputs with versioned datasets and explicit scorers.
sources.does_not_support: Treating a trace as proof that an explanation is correct, treating structured output as evidence fidelity, or enabling a model that failed local deterministic and practitioner gates.
